latin.317:
HEXAS ANNOTATIONUM IN CONTROVERSIAS PROTESTANTICAS PRIORES
DE COENA DOMINI, UNDE INITIUM SCHISMATIS,
ANNOTATIO I
De Sensu verborum Institutionis Sacrae Coenae, proprio ne, an figurato?
§. I.
Cur Controversiae Protestanticæ de Coena Domini, Autori nostro Priores dicantur, ipsemet haud obscurè subinnuit, quando subjicit: unde Schismatis initium.
latin.318: Scilicet priores audiunt, non prioritate Dignitatis, quòd fundamentalem quendam fidei Christianae articulum, aut principalem istorum concernunt qui sub disputationes incudem à Protestantibus, & inter se, revocantur; nec Prioritate Ordinis, quòd in Methodica, id est, juxta naturalem Systematis Theologici methodum disposita Controversiarum Protestanticarum tractatione, primum locum mererentur. Has enim prioritatis species vel Lutheranorum nonnulli deprecabuntur, per rationes plurimas ab And. Sennerto in unum collectas, Exerc. Theol. de articulis fid. fundamentalibus §. 64. & 65. p. Fasciculi exercitationum ejus 430. & 431.
latin.319: Sed verò prioritate partim temporis, quòd Babylone pontificiâ egressi, primò omnium, in nonnullis de Coena Domini quaestionibus, à se invicem dissentire coeperint Protestantes;
latin.320: partim acerbitatis, quòd dissensus hic in nervum tandem erupit, ut schismati Protestantico turpe dederit initium.
latin.321: Prioris Prioritatis occasionem non insulsè annotat B. Georg. Calixtus hisce verbis: Sacramentum Eucharistiae multis & tetris abusibus & superstitionibus hactenus apud Pontificios deformatum erat & vix aliud religionis caput parem calamitatem expertum: Panem benedictum abusu remoto, quod nihil nisi ipsumissimum corpus crederent esse, adorabant & vulgò adorandum proponebant, quin & sacrificium propitiatorium (vocabulo hôc strictè & in formali significatione accepto) habebant & offerebant. Atque adeo Missas ut vocant solitarias, Communicantium expertes, frequentissimè celebrabant, rarò autem adhibitis Communicantibus. Hisce erroribus & pravitatibus abolendis intenti erant primi Reformationis duces & Autores, quod omnino rectè erat; quae est autem humani ingenii imbecillitas, quomodo id rectè fieret, non omnes in istis initiis providebant, Judic. de controversiis theologicis §.47. Batav. ed. p. 69. in fine & 70.
latin.322: Posterioris Prioritatis Causam Autoremque Lutherum vel ipse Lutheranus Dav. Chytraeus memorat, quando in actis suis cum Zwinglianis, colloquio Marpurgensi inter Protestantes, anno 1529. habito & à se plenè recitato tandem subjicit: Postquam igitur in colloquio Marpurgensi D. Lutherus, Zwinglium, Oecolampadium, Bucerum & eorum socios propterea quod in articulo de vera & essentiali praesentia corporis & sanguinis Christi in Coena Domini, diversum à sententia sua docerent, pro fratribus agnoscere & recipere noluit, Landgravius tamen & alii boni & pacis ac concordiae cupidi non destiterunt in eo elaborare, ut dissensio illa de Coena Domini piè componi & leniri & Christiana pax & fraternitas inter utramque partem constitui posset. p. mihi 647.

pass_a.317: HEXAD OF ANNOTATIONS ON THE PRIOR PROTESTANT CONTROVERSIES CONCERNING THE LORD’S SUPPER, WHENCE THE BEGINNING OF THE SCHISM. ANNOTATION I. On the Sense of the words of Institution of the Sacred Supper — whether proper, or figurative? §. I. Why the Protestant Controversies on the Lord’s Supper are called Priores by our Author, he himself not obscurely hints when he adds: whence the beginning of the Schism.
pass_a.318: Namely they are heard as prior, not by priority of Dignity — because they concern some fundamental article of the Christian faith, or a principal one of those brought back under the anvil of disputations by Protestants and among themselves; nor by Priority of Order — because in a Methodical treatment of Protestant Controversies, that is disposed according to the natural method of the Theological System, they would deserve first place. For even some of the Lutherans will deprecate these species of priority, by many reasons collected into one by And. Sennert, Theological Exercises on the fundamental articles of faith §§. 64 & 65, pp. 430 & 431 of his Fascicle of exercises.
pass_a.319: But truly by priority partly of time — because, having gone out from papal Babylon, Protestants first of all began to dissent from one another in some questions concerning the Lord’s Supper;
pass_a.320: partly of acerbitas — because this dissent at last erupted into the nerve, so that it gave a foul beginning to the Protestant schism.
pass_a.321: The occasion of the Prior Priority B. Georg. Calixtus not tastelessly annotates in these words: The Sacrament of the Eucharist had hitherto been deformed among the Pontificians by many and foul abuses and superstitions, and scarcely any other head of religion had experienced equal calamity: they adored the blessed bread — the abuse removed — because they believed it to be nothing but the very Body itself, and commonly set it forth to be adored; nay they also held and offered a propitiatory sacrifice (the word taken strictly and in its formal signification). And so they most frequently celebrated solitary Masses, as they call them, devoid of Communicants, and rarely with Communicants admitted. The first leaders and Authors of the Reformation were intent on abolishing these errors and pravities, which was altogether right; but such is the weakness of human ingenuity that not all foresaw in those beginnings how that would rightly be done — Judgment on theological controversies §.47, Dutch ed. p. 69 at the end & 70.
pass_a.322: The Cause and Author of the Posterior Priority even the Lutheran David Chytraeus himself records, when in his acts with the Zwinglians, in the Marburg colloquy held among Protestants in the year 1529 and fully recited by him, he at last adds: After therefore in the Marburg colloquy Dr. Luther was unwilling to acknowledge and receive as brothers Zwingli, Oecolampadius, Bucer and their associates, because on the article of the true and essential presence of the body and blood of Christ in the Lord’s Supper they taught differently from his opinion, nevertheless the Landgrave and other good men eager for peace and concord did not cease to labor that that dissent on the Lord’s Supper might be piously composed and softened and Christian peace and fraternity established between both parties. p. to me 647.

317: Here begins the Hexad of Annotations on the earlier Protestant fights over the Lord’s Supper — the place where the schism took its start.
ANNOTATION I asks whether the Institution words of the Sacred Supper are to be taken properly or figuratively.
§. I. Our author himself shows why he calls those Supper controversies Priores when he adds the clause: whence the beginning of the Schism.
318: They are not “prior” by dignity — as if they alone were some fundamental article of the faith, or the chief matter Protestants hammer out among themselves.
Nor by order — as if a methodical theological system would have to put them first.
Even some Lutherans deprecate those kinds of priority (Sennert, Exercises on fundamental articles §§. 64–65, fasc. pp. 430–431).
319: They are prior partly by time.
Once out of papal Babylon, Protestants first began to dissent from one another on some questions about the Lord’s Supper.
320: They are prior partly by acerbitas.
That dissent at last erupted into the nerve and gave a foul beginning to the Protestant schism.
321: Calixtus notes the occasion of that first priority without tastelessness: among the Pontificians the Eucharist had been deformed by foul abuses and superstitions — scarcely any other head of religion had suffered equal calamity.
They adored the blessed bread as the very Body, set it out for adoration, and offered a propitiatory sacrifice; solitary Masses without communicants were frequent.
The first Reformation leaders rightly meant to abolish those errors — yet human ingenuity is weak, and not all foresaw at the start how it would be done rightly (Judic. §.47, Dutch ed. pp. 69–70).
322: Even the Lutheran David Chytraeus records the cause and author of the second priority.

In his full account of the 1529 Marburg colloquy he adds: after Luther refused to acknowledge Zwingli, Oecolampadius, Bucer and their associates as brothers — because they taught differently on the true and essential presence of Christ’s body and blood in the Supper —
the Landgrave and other peace-seekers still did not stop laboring that the Supper dissent might be piously softened and Christian peace and fraternity set between both sides (p. mihi 647).
Stop before §. II (first controversy: interpretation of the Institution words Hoc est corpus meum — literal/κατὰ τὸ ῥητόν vs proper/improper).
